Claude Opus 5.description: Anthropic's advanced model for complex agentic coding, deep reasoning, and enterprise work. It has a one-million-token context window, up to 128K output tokens, and thinking enabled by default.
features: Strong long-horizon coding and deep reasoning
Current advanced Claude tier below Fable 5

Claude Opus 4.8.description: Anthropic's previous Opus model. It remains available, but use Claude Opus 5 for new complex agentic coding and enterprise work.
features: Strong complex reasoning and agentic coding
Good for detailed writing and editing

Claude Sonnet 5.description: Anthropic's speed-and-intelligence option for day-to-day agents, coding, writing, and interactive work. Product defaults vary, so select a model alias or exact ID when reproducibility matters.
features: Best for expressive writing and brainstorming

Claude Haiku 4.5.description: Anthropic's fastest and cheapest model. Haiku 4.5 delivers near-frontier performance for high-volume, cost-sensitive tasks like classification, extraction, and quick Q&A.
features: Lowest per-token cost in the Claude family
Great for batch processing and high-volume workflows

Claude Fable 5.description: Anthropic's most capable broadly released model for long-running agents and difficult work. Use it when you need maximum capability and can accept higher latency and cost.
features: Highest-capability Claude option in the current catalog
Useful for difficult research, coding, and synthesis

Gemini 3.1 Pro.description: Google's preview reasoning model for difficult multimodal and long-context work. Preview status can change, so check the model lifecycle page before production use.
features: Better multimodal synthesis (text, images, audio, video)
Preview model: verify availability before deployment

Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite.description: Google's cheapest Gemini tier. Flash-Lite retains a long context window and runs even faster than Flash, making it a natural fit for high-volume agentic calls and cost-sensitive background automations.

Gemini 3.7 Flash.description: Google's newest and most intelligent Flash workhorse for coding and agents. It is available through the Gemini API and current Google agent products; verify rollout and regional availability before production deployment.
features: Optimized for coding and agent workflows
Multimodal input and built-in tool support

Gemini 3.6 Flash.description: Google's previous stable Flash workhorse. It remains useful for qualified production integrations, but Gemini 3.7 Flash is the current recommendation for new coding and agent work.
features: Strong multimodal input and tool use
Good for interactive agents and high-throughput workflows

Gemini 3.5 Flash.description: An earlier stable Gemini Flash tier for sustained agentic, coding, and multimodal work. Prefer Gemini 3.7 Flash for new work unless an existing integration requires this version.
features: Earlier stable tier for sustained agentic work

Veo 3.1.description: Google's current Veo video-generation family. Availability and supported controls vary by product and API, so confirm the exact model and terms before production use.
features: Native video and audio generation options

Gemini 2.5 Pro (legacy).description: Google's previous-generation 'work' model. While still capable, Gemini 3.1 Pro is recommended for new work due to its improved reasoning and efficiency.

Gemini 2.5 Flash (legacy).description: Google's previous-generation fast model. Gemini 3.7 Flash is recommended for new work due to newer coding and agent capabilities.

GPT-5.6 Sol.description: OpenAI's recommended flagship for complex reasoning and agentic work. The GPT-5.6 alias resolves to Sol; pin an exact snapshot only when reproducibility is more important than automatic upgrades.
features: 1.05M-token context and up to 128K output tokens

GPT-5.6 Terra.description: OpenAI's balanced GPT-5.6 tier for capable everyday agents, coding, and knowledge work at lower latency and cost than Sol.
features: Suitable for daily agent and coding work
Part of the current GPT-5.6 family

GPT-5.6 Luna.description: OpenAI's fastest and most economical GPT-5.6 tier for routine work, high-throughput tasks, and responsive applications.
features: Part of the current GPT-5.6 family

GPT 5.4.description: An older supported OpenAI flagship. Prefer GPT-5.6 Sol for new complex agent work, or GPT-5.6 Terra/Luna when latency and cost matter more.
features: Useful where an existing integration is already qualified

Codex (GPT-5.6 Sol).description: OpenAI's coding-agent experience using GPT-5.6 Sol for complex repository work. Use explicit approval boundaries, relevant tool subsets, bounded concurrency, tests, and exact-head review gates.

Nano Banana 2.description: Google's current all-around image model, exposed as Gemini 3.1 Flash Image. Use Nano Banana 2 Lite for lower latency and cost, or Nano Banana Pro for the most complex image work.

NotebookLM.description: Google's research and writing assistant that is grounded in your chosen source documents. It helps you get summaries, ask questions, and generate ideas based only on the material you provide, reducing hallucinations.
features: Generates summaries, FAQs, and audio overviews
Excellent for analyzing collections of documents

Grok 4.5.description: SpaceXAI's current frontier model, published through the x.ai developer domain. Current web or X information requires enabling the Web Search or X Search tool; the base model is not automatically real-time.
features: Optional Web Search and X Search tools
Useful for research when sources are independently verified

Perplexity.description: Perplexity's current Sonar family combines web search with generated answers. Use Sonar for quick grounded queries, Sonar Pro for more complex follow-ups, Sonar Reasoning Pro for multi-step analysis, and Sonar Deep Research for long reports.
features: Provides answers with inline source citations
Separate search, reasoning, and deep-research tiers
Useful for source discovery and initial research
Verify cited primary sources before publication

Open-weight models.description: A category of models whose weights are available for local or private deployment. Licenses differ, and open weights do not always mean open source. Check each model's license, hardware needs, and safety controls before use.
features: Can run on local hardware (via Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM)
Current options include Kimi K3, GLM-5.2, DeepSeek V4, Qwen, MiniMax M3, Mistral, StepFun, MiMo, Hy3, Command A+, Nemotron 3 Ultra, and Llama 4
No per-token costs once running locally

GLM-5.2 (open weights).description: Z.ai's MIT-licensed open-weight model for long-horizon agentic work, with a one-million-token context option. Hardware and provider behavior vary, so benchmark it on your own workload.
features: Current open-weight option for long-horizon agents

Qwen 3.7 Plus.description: Alibaba Cloud's current hosted Qwen Plus tier for long-context agents and multimodal knowledge work. The moving alias currently provides a one-million-token context window.

Qwen 3.8 Max (preview).description: Alibaba Cloud's newest preview Qwen reasoning tier. Use it for evaluations that need the highest hosted Qwen capability, but keep production work on a stable model until its lifecycle and terms are suitable.
features: Reasoning, text generation, and agent workflows

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (open weights).description: Alibaba's open-weight mixture-of-experts model with 35B total and about 3B active parameters. It is a practical efficiency-oriented option for local agentic coding and general tool use.
features: Good for IDE autocomplete and refactoring

DeepSeek V4 (open weights).description: DeepSeek V4 Pro and Flash are MIT-licensed open-weight models with one-million-token context. Choose Pro for maximum capability or Flash for lower latency, and migrate away from deprecated deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner aliases.
features: Open weights and hosted API options

Kimi K3 (open weights).description: Moonshot AI's current open-weight flagship for long-horizon coding, visual understanding, and end-to-end knowledge work. The hosted model and released weights support a one-million-token context window.
features: Custom Kimi K3 License requires use-case review

MiniMax M3.description: MiniMax's open-weight frontier coding and agent model with native multimodal input and up to one million tokens of context. The published weights use the MiniMax Community License.

Mistral Medium 3.5 (open weights).description: Mistral's frontier-class multimodal model for agentic and coding work. It supports a 256K context window and uses a Modified MIT license.

NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra (open weights).description: NVIDIA's open model for long-running agent orchestration. It uses a 550B-parameter mixture-of-experts design with 55B active parameters and supports up to one million tokens of context.
features: Open weights, recipes, and deployment tooling

Mistral Small 4 (open weights).description: Mistral's efficient hybrid model for instruction following, reasoning, and coding. It supports a 256K context window and uses the Apache 2.0 license.
features: Unified instruct, reasoning, and coding modes

Step-3.7-Flash (open weights).description: StepFun's current efficient agentic model. It targets coding, tool use, and research workflows and is released under the Apache 2.0 license.

MiMo-V2-Flash (open weights).description: Xiaomi's efficient reasoning, coding, and agent model. It has 309B total parameters, 15B active parameters, and a 256K context window.

Tencent Hy3 (open weights).description: Tencent Hunyuan's efficient reasoning and agent model. The released Hy3 family uses a mixture-of-experts design with 295B total and 21B active parameters.
features: Benchmark on the target inference stack

Cohere Command A+ (open weights).description: Cohere's current multimodal enterprise agent model. It supports reasoning, tool use, translation across 48 languages, 128K context, and private deployment under Apache 2.0.

Llama 4 Scout / Maverick (open weights).description: Meta's latest released Llama language-model family. Scout prioritizes efficient deployment and very long context; Maverick provides the stronger general-purpose multimodal tier.
features: Scout supports up to 10M input tokens
Maverick is the higher-capability released tier

ERNIE 5.1.description: Baidu's current ERNIE general model, released in May 2026. It focuses on writing, understanding, reasoning, and agent tasks in Baidu's hosted products.

ByteDance Seed2.0.description: ByteDance's current general multimodal and agent model family. Seed2.0 Pro and Code are available in Doubao and TRAE, with APIs through Volcano Engine.

ElevenLabs.description: ElevenLabs provides speech, transcription, sound, and music models. Eleven v3 is the most expressive speech model; Flash v2.5 is the low-latency choice; Multilingual v2 remains the stable long-form option; Scribe v2 handles transcription; Music v2 is the current music model.
features: Eleven v3 expressive speech and multi-speaker dialogue
Scribe v2 and Scribe v2 Realtime for transcription
Music v2 for prompted music generation
Voice cloning requires consent and policy checks

Midjourney.description: Midjourney's newest image model is V8.2, released July 24, 2026. V8.1 became the default in June; V8.2 improves aesthetics, image quality, and personalization.
features: Review editorial disclosure and synthetic-media policy before publication
